labor-sheds.name: Labor Sheds
labor-sheds.narrative: Two numbers on this page change what a shed costs and how it performs, and neither is obvious from a photograph. The first is the floor: an RCC slab rather than a board platform is what lets a hall take dense bed rows and daily wet cleaning for years. The second is the ventilation build-up: a continuous louvre band integrated into the wall, working with a ridge ventilator, is what keeps a single large volume habitable without power. When you compare quotations line by line, compare those two first.

prefab-site-canteen.name: Prefab Site Canteen
prefab-site-canteen.narrative: Two lines in the tables below change what you actually buy. The first is that the floor and wall finishes split by zone, so a dining wall and a wash-area wall are not the same specification and are not priced as though they were. The second is that the roof exhaust package is conditional: a dining-only canteen does not inherit a heavy kitchen hood, and a canteen with a cookline needs one engineered before manufacture rather than cut in afterwards.

oil-field-camp.narrative: Two lines in these tables change more for a buyer than the rest combined. The first is the floor frame: a lift-and-carry skid with runner beams is what makes the building relocatable, and it is why the transport drawing, not the floor plan, governs how the unit may be handled. The second is ventilation and AC: the base module is normal-area, so a location with a classified hazardous area needs a separate engineered package, priced against your own classification document. Everything else in Table 1 supports the first of those, and most of Table 2 supports the second.

specifications.meaning: Clearances preserve cleaning and emergency assistance; accessible cubicles follow project-required openings

specifications.group: Openings, Services, Layout, Finish and Handover
specifications.detail: High-level privacy ventilation openings
specifications.scopeClass: High-level louvres or frosted windows with insect protection, plus mechanical exhaust openings sized to wet load and privacy requirement
specifications.meaning: Openings avoid direct sightlines while supporting airflow

specifications.group: Openings, Services, Layout, Finish and Handover
specifications.detail: Security grille, insect screen and privacy accessories
specifications.scopeClass: Removable mesh, louvres, restrictors, privacy screens or protected MS grilles only where room use and the approved opening schedule require
specifications.meaning: Ventilation, cleaning access and emergency escape are maintained

specifications.group: Openings, Services, Layout, Finish and Handover
specifications.detail: Copper wiring and labelled containment
specifications.scopeClass: Typical references 1.5 sq mm lighting, 2.5 sq mm sockets, 4 sq mm high-load; final sizing follows connected load, voltage drop and protection coordination
specifications.meaning: FR/FRLS copper in conduit, separated from water and waste routes

specifications.group: Openings, Services, Layout, Finish and Handover
specifications.detail: Distribution, residual-current protection and earthing
specifications.scopeClass: Main isolator, MCB / RCBO or RCCB protection, labelled neutral and earth bars, bonding, surge protection where required
specifications.meaning: Frame and exposed conductive parts bond to the tested site earth; this workbook does not certify the installation

specifications.group: Openings, Services, Layout, Finish and Handover
specifications.detail: Fixed lights, fans, sockets and service points
specifications.scopeClass: LED luminaires, fan points, 6A/16A sockets, exhaust points and emergency lighting only in the quantities on the approved schedule
specifications.meaning: Loose appliances, AC units and DG or UPS equipment are excluded unless itemised

specifications.group: Openings, Services, Layout, Finish and Handover
specifications.detail: Continuous wet-area exhaust strategy
specifications.scopeClass: Natural high-level ventilation supplemented by exhaust fans and ducts as needed; quantity and airflow sized from cubicle and shower load against room volume
specifications.meaning: Air-change values and controls are project decisions, not workbook values

specifications.group: Openings, Services, Layout, Finish and Handover
specifications.detail: Multi-fixture plumbing manifold
specifications.scopeClass: CPVC or PPR supply, uPVC soil, waste and vent, isolation by bank, WCs, urinals, basins and showers per the fixture schedule, floor drains, traps and external sewer or holding-tank connection
specifications.meaning: Fixture count is not inferred from area; tender and applicable site rules set ratios, gender split and storage

specifications.group: Openings, Services, Layout, Finish and Handover
specifications.detail: Ablution bank and maintenance layout
specifications.scopeClass: Repeated toilet, shower and basin banks with dry entry, privacy segregation, central or service-side pipe access and cleaning circulation; accessible cubicle where the project requires it
specifications.meaning: Resolves headcount, shifts, gender, pressure, drainage level and maintenance access; distinct from a single attached-toilet cabin

specifications.group: Openings, Services, Layout, Finish and Handover
specifications.detail: Corrosion protection and external finish
specifications.scopeClass: Prepared carbon steel with compatible primer and top coats, or galvanized / pre-painted sheet with repaired cut edges; upgraded for coastal, industrial or wet-service exposure
specifications.meaning: Skid undersides, roof drains, cut edges and wet thresholds govern field durability

specifications.group: Openings, Services, Layout, Finish and Handover
specifications.detail: Factory and site QA and handover evidence
specifications.scopeClass: Dimensional, member, weld and bolt, coating, panel, roof-drainage, opening, electrical and plumbing checks plus wet-test checks
specifications.meaning: Handover evidence identifies the approved GA, BOM, test records and maintenance points

specifications.group: Openings, Services, Layout, Finish and Handover
specifications.detail: Contract-controlled warranty and maintenance obligations
specifications.scopeClass: Period, start date, remedy, relocation conditions, consumables and exclusions exactly as the signed quotation and handover documents state
specifications.meaning: Site foundations, utilities, misuse, blocked drains and missed maintenance remain excluded unless expressly covered

ablution-block.narrative: Read these two tables as one decision rather than two lists. The first table sets what the building is: the frame that carries wet loads and lifting, and the envelope that has to stay washable and keep water out of insulation and steel. The second sets how it works day to day: the openings that give privacy and airflow, the manifold you will isolate and maintain, and the boundary where SAMAN's supply stops. Where a line says the final value follows the approved drawing, that is not evasion. It means the value is set for your site rather than assumed here.
